5.17.7.en: * To serve Christ is to serve wisdom, which is the service of righteousness, and the service of truth and all the virtues related to it.

5.18.0.en: Origen: He will take holiness as an invincible shield. [19]

5.18.1.en: How is holiness counted an invincible shield?

5.18.2.en: The words “holiness,” “saint,” and “holy” are taken from the Greek “hagios,” and carry the meaning of withdrawal from what is earthly, that is, there is no place for the earth in the person. This is the negative side. As for the positive, God is holy, that is, in Him is all fullness, and He needs nothing outside Himself. The saint is one who possesses this Holy One who fills his whole inner being, so that he never feels emptiness; the world has no place in his depths, but God fills all his heart, his feelings and his senses.

5.18.3.en: The wise man portrays the believer as a good spiritual soldier who bears the weapons of righteousness and enjoys the crown of victory and triumph, receiving it from the hand of the Lord Himself; and at the same time he does not ascribe the victory to himself, but hides himself in the right hand of the Lord and takes shelter in His divine arm. Now that he has put on the whole armor of God, of which the Apostle Paul spoke in his Epistle to the Ephesians 6:10-18, the Lord gives him His divine zeal working in him, as though He were arming His creation so that it might be sheltered from the devil, who bears a spirit of enmity against the Lord Himself.

5.18.4.en: In other words, if the Lord arms His human creation, He does not want it to enter the battle as a party; rather the Lord Himself enters through it to shatter the opposing devil.

5.19.0.en: He will sharpen (make keen) His unyielding wrath into a sword, and the world shall fight with Him against the unwise. [20]

5.19.1.en: God’s surpassing love toward mankind does not mean that He is lenient with the wicked or indulgent toward them, for He cannot bear sin and evil.

5.19.2.en: The holy God uses His creation, whether heavenly or earthly, to discipline the wicked here on earth. As for the day of judgment, St. Jacob of Serugh sees that God will set up the Apostles to judge, not from themselves or according to their own thoughts, but according to the mind of God, whose glory the wicked will not see, so that they may not enjoy it and so that they may not ask for His mercy. I referred to this in my comments on the first phrase of this chapter.

5.20.0.en: Then the lightnings go forth like well-aimed arrows, and from the clouds, as from a well-strung bow, they fly to the mark. [21]

5.20.1.en: The Holy Bible often portrays inanimate nature moving to bear witness to its holy Creator, and standing in enmity against the foolish wicked.

5.20.2.en: The wise man sees that the lightnings have turned into arrows in the hand of the Creator, which He aims against evil and the wicked, releasing them from among the clouds, as arrows are released from the bow.

5.20.3.en: Here he presents different images of nature’s revolt against the wicked who resist the holy Creator. They are like blows that fall upon them to reveal the corruption and ruin within them:

5.22.0.en: d. A flood of merciless rivers [23].

5.22.2.en: The purpose of these blows and others is that man may discover the reality of his depths, that perhaps he may realize the danger he has reached, and return to the Creator, the Savior of souls.

5.22.3.en: The lightnings aimed from the clouds like arrows symbolize the man who casts from his mouth arrows of deceit and falsehood, so that their tongues are arrows filled with deadly poison. Warriors used to smear arrows with poisonous substances, so that when they pierced a man’s body they poisoned him at once.

5.22.4.en: And the hail falling like stones and killing the grass signifies the ruin of man’s heart, that is, the Lord’s vineyard; instead of being watered with the waters of the Spirit to bear satisfying spiritual trees, the heart turns into a fallow land full of weeds, which the hail kills.

5.22.5.en: And the raging waves signify souls that know no peace and calm, but are in a state of constant turmoil.

5.22.6.en: And the flood of rivers signifies extremism in everything, so that man does not walk in wisdom and perishes because of his extremism.

5.22.7.en: As for the sandstorms, they signify the heart that has not received the waters of the Spirit, and so turns into a deadly wilderness.

5.22.8.en: Nature’s revolt begins with lightnings accompanied by thunder, and Origen sees in the thunder and lightning a reference to the divine teachings that come from heaven, by which man is disciplined so that he may recognize his faults.

5.22.9.en: * “He sent out His arrows, and scattered them” (Ps 18:14). He sent out the Evangelists to cross straight roads on wings of power, not by their own strength, but by the power of Him who sent them. “And scattered them,” among those to whom He sent them, that they might be to some the savour of life unto life, and to others the savour of death unto death (2 Cor 2:16). “And many lightnings, and troubled them” (Ps 18:14), for He multiplied wonders and troubled them.

5.22.10.en: St. Augustine: And hailstones full of wrath shall be cast as from a sling, and the water of the sea shall rage against them, and the floods shall cruelly drown them. [22]

5.22.11.en: Since the wicked man does not listen to the voice of the heavenly teachings and accept their illumination, being indifferent to the thunder and the lightnings, the blow of hail comes upon him, falling from heaven like heavy stones, as though cast from on high upon their crops and their animals, and even upon themselves. As the Psalmist says: “He destroyed their beasts with hail, and their cattle with lightnings” (Ps 78:47-48).

5.22.12.en: The hail that kills the crops falls bearing the signs of wrath against evil, as though it were missiles skillfully directed.

5.22.13.en: And the sea also declares its wrath and rages, and the waves rise against the wicked.

5.22.14.en: And the rivers that water the crops, the animals and men overflow to destroy with their flood without mercy.

5.22.15.en: As we stand here before the missiles that come with the hail, we remember the plague of the Egyptians concerning hail and fire together. “And the LORD gave thunder and hail, and the fire ran along upon the ground; and the LORD rained hail upon the land of Egypt. So there was hail, and fire continuing in the midst of the hail, a very great thing, such as there was none like it in all the land of Egypt since it became a nation” (Ex 9:24-25). St. Mar Ephraim the Syrian has a comment on this strange sight.

5.22.16.en: * Hail and fire fell together. The hail did not quench the fire, nor did the fire melt the hail, as it would in thickets; and the hail turned red like iron in the fire, blazing in the hail.

5.22.17.en: * By the sounds of thunder and lightning, the Lord punished the Egyptians who enslaved His people. And Christ, by His twelve Apostles and by the voices of His teachings, punished the demons.

5.22.18.en: From heaven the sounds of thunder frightened the Egyptians; and the holy Apostles, by their heavenly teachings, cried out and frightened the demons.

5.22.19.en: The Lord struck the Egyptians with hail and fire. And this great wonder, that fire and water were mingled, was a plague for the Egyptians. And Christ, by His holy Apostles, struck the demons with the waters of holy Baptism, in which water and the fire of the Holy Spirit are gathered together. The water is for washing the filth of the body, and the fire of the Holy Spirit for washing the filth of the soul...

5.22.20.en: The baptism of the Spirit, if one may say so, is the hail and fire with which Christ strikes the demons at all times by the hand of His disciples and their successors forever.

5.22.21.en: St. Mar Ephraim the Syrian: St. Augustine sees that the deadly plague of hail is man’s loss of his love for his brother, for it places him in a severe coldness of heart in the midst of the darkness of the night of ignorance.

5.22.22.en: He concludes his discourse on the blows that will befall the wicked on earth with a dangerous wind that blows upon them, scattering them like a whirlwind, and turns their life, which became earth and not heaven, into a wilderness, depriving them of what they considered thrones and honors.

5.22.23.en: In the interpretation of St. Hippolytus of Rome for the destructive east wind (Hos 13:15), he sees that it is against the Antichrist, who appears in the last days to ensnare, if possible, even the elect, so that they go astray from the truth.

5.22.24.en: * What is this scorching wind coming from the east, which dries up the courses of water and the fruit of the trees in his time, when the people put their heart in his works? For they worship him in his corruption.

5.22.25.en: St. Hippolytus: Theodoret, bishop of Cyrrhus, relates what happened in his days in the war of the year 441 A.D., saying: [This is what happened in our time, for in the war that took place recently, He destroyed with hail and fire the savages coming from the north to attack us. Recently the Persians stirred up a war against us from the east, and they expected to seize our cities without shedding blood, but some of them died, and others were driven away to bring reports of what had happened.]

5.22.26.en: And a mighty wind shall blow upon them, and scatter them like a whirlwind.

5.22.27.en: And iniquity shall make the whole earth a wilderness, and the committing of evils shall overthrow the thrones of the mighty. [23]

5.22.28.en: The earth turns into a desolate desert full of destructive whirlwinds and sandstorms.

5.22.29.en: Take me into Your ship, and I shall be saved!

5.22.30.en: * My soul longs for the day of Your coming!

5.22.31.en: Your children stand with boldness before those who mocked them and troubled them!

5.22.32.en: They see You, and Your splendor is reflected upon them; they cleave to You as a heavenly procession, and enjoy eternal glories!

5.22.35.en: Your coming becomes misery for them.

5.22.36.en: They look at Your children and are dismayed!

5.22.37.en: They are astonished at the salvation of Your sons, which they despised and did not expect!

5.22.38.en: * They repent and sigh, and confess that they were foolish!

5.22.39.en: In the thick darkness each one of them rebukes the other, but none of them is any longer able to look upon the Sun of Righteousness.

5.22.40.en: * They cry out, confessing that they chose iniquity and corruption, and despised the way of the Lord!

5.22.41.en: They lost everything, even their lives!

5.22.42.en: Their pleasures turned into a cause of eternal bitterness!

5.22.43.en: Their arrogance turned into indescribable humiliation!

5.22.44.en: Their temporal life on earth passed away, and they were not able to acquire a portion with the heavenly ones!

5.22.45.en: * Now I cry out to You, my God, before it is too late.

5.22.46.en: Grant me to know You with the righteous, O divine Truth, that my whole life may not become like a passing and vain shadow!

5.22.47.en: Grant me to be a light cloud that carries You, and not the shadow of a cloud that goes and does not return. Record my name in Your book with Your sons, that my life may not become like a rumor that passes and vanishes.

5.22.48.en: Take me into Your ship that I may be saved, and let me not stand occupied with the trace of its passage amid the waves, without entering into it.

5.22.49.en: Grant me the wings of Your Holy Spirit, that I may fly and be with You in heaven, and not stand as a spectator looking at Your saints like flying doves!

5.22.50.en: Aim the arrow of Your love into my heart, that my soul may cry out in song:

5.22.52.en: The wounds of Your love heal me and comfort me.

5.22.53.en: Let Your divine arrow enter into my depths, and let me not be occupied with theoretical inquiry into its passage through the air.

5.22.54.en: * Grant me the weapons of the Spirit, O divine Commander.

5.22.55.en: Then I enter the battle with You, and the devil, the enemy, falls like lightning from heaven.

5.22.56.en: I enjoy Your eternal Kingdom, and I am adorned with the crown that Your hands offer me.

5.22.57.en: In You alone I triumph and am crowned; in Your right hand You shelter me by Your grace, and with Your arms outstretched on the Cross You protect me and embrace me.

5.22.58.en: * My God, Your teachings thunder in my heart, and I am filled with fear of You mingled with love.

5.22.59.en: May You cast hail upon my sins and destroy them, that they may have no authority over me!

5.22.60.en: May You allow the waves of the seas to calm, that I may enjoy Your heavenly peace.

5.22.61.en: I no longer fear the flood, for I am with Noah inside the ark.

5.22.62.en: Nor am I troubled by the sandstorms, for You have turned my wilderness into a closed garden, which the whirlwinds of the world cannot approach and storm.

5.22.63.en: To You be glory, O You who are wonderful in His gifts!

6.0.s.en: 1. A final warning to the leaders

6.0.0.en: 1 Wisdom is better than strength, and the wise man better than the mighty. 2 And you, O kings, hear and understand, and O judges of the ends of the earth, be admonished. 3 Give heed, you who rule over the multitudes, who boast in the crowds of the nations, 4 for your authority is from the Lord, and your power from the Most High, who will examine your works, and search out your intentions. 5 For you, being servants of His kingdom, have not judged with the judgment of truth, nor kept the Law, nor walked according to the will of God. 6 He will come upon you suddenly with a terrifying appearing, for a severe judgment will be executed upon the rulers. 7 For the small one is worthy of mercy, but the mighty are examined with might. 8 And the Lord of all makes no exception of anyone, nor stands in awe of greatness, for both the small and the great are His making alike, and His care extends to all. 9 But for the strong there is a severe trial. 10 To you, O kings, my words are directed, that you may learn wisdom and not fall. 11 For those who keep in holiness what is holy shall be sanctified, and those who learn these things find what to say in defense. 12 Therefore desire my words, and be zealous for them, and you shall be instructed.

6.0.1.en: Hear then, O kings, and understand!

6.0.2.en: And learn, O judges of the ends of the earth! [1]

6.0.3.en: Solomon returns to affirm that he directs his words to kings, judges, and those who hold authority and temporal honors, as the Book began. And as we said at the beginning of the Book, the discourse is directed to every human being, because God created mankind to be kings and great ones and holders of authority. Man was not created to be a slave or to live in humiliation, but when humanity entered the circle of sin it fell under its law, which is exploitation and tyranny and disregard for the rights of others and their dignity. So it befits the believer, whatever his position, abilities or possibilities, to remember what God created him to be as one with authority, and to look upon every human being, even if he is a small child or one afflicted with some infirmity, as a person who has his dignity and esteem even in the eyes of God Himself.

6.1.0.en: Give ear, you who rule over the multitudes, and who boast in the multitude of your nations! [2]

6.1.1.en: The wise man often fears the misuse of authority, whether civil or religious, and so he links it with fatherhood and love toward those who are subject to them.

6.1.2.en: St. John Chrysostom makes clear that slavery is not in God’s original plan.

6.1.3.en: And the Cappadocian theologian St. Gregory of Nazianzus declares that slavery is a wicked discrimination between human beings, and yet it is part of the present reality.

6.1.4.en: In the same spirit St. Basil the Great says that no one is by nature a slave. But at the same time he did not call for resisting the order of society, for he says: [Even if one man is made a master and another a slave, yet through our view of equality in rank, we are all a flock of our Creator, brothers and slaves.]

6.1.5.en: If this is what befits civil leaders, how much more does it befit spiritual leaders to be loving fathers, supporting their children by every means, and not holders of authority who command and lord it over them.

6.1.6.en: * “And though you have ten thousand instructors... yet not many fathers” (1 Cor 15:4)... Paul does not here seek any honor, but rather shows the depth of his love. For honor belongs to the instructor, and love is the mark of the father.

6.1.7.en: * You have seen a man (the Apostle Paul) who traveled the whole earth, because his ambition and aim were to lead every person to God. And he fulfilled this ambition with all the strength he had stored up, as though the whole world had become his children; therefore he was in haste.

6.1.8.en: He was always traveling, always zealous to call all humanity to the Kingdom of Heaven, offering care, counsel, promises, prayer and help, and rebuking demons, driving out the spirits that insisted on destruction.

6.1.9.en: He used his personal abilities and his appearance, and letters, preaching, works, disciples, and the raising up of the fallen by his own effort. He supported those who strive that they might stand firm in their striving, and raised up everyone who was cast down fallen on the ground.

6.1.10.en: He guided the penitent, comforted the suffering, warned the offenders, and strictly watched over the resisters and opponents.

6.1.11.en: He shared as leader and healing physician in the struggle, and stretched out a hand of help to attack or defend or guide as need required in the field of work, so that he was everything to those engaged in the struggle...

6.1.12.en: In his greatness he was more ardent and zealous than any flame of fire. And as for the crown of all the virtues, he surpassed (all the virtues) in love. And as iron melts in the fire and all becomes burning fire, so Paul melted in love, until he himself became love incarnate.

6.1.13.en: He became as though a father to the whole world. His love rivaled the love of fathers according to the flesh, or rather surpassed them all in love, bodily and spiritual, and in concern and care, giving all his wealth, his words, his body and his spirit, indeed his whole being, for those whom he loved.

6.2.0.en: St. John Chrysostom: For your authority was given to you from the Lord, and your sovereignty from the Most High, who shall examine your works, and search out your counsels. [3]

6.2.1.en: David his father had already asked the kings to be wise, that is, to walk with understanding, wisdom and discipline, and asks them to serve the Lord with fear and rejoicing. “Be wise now therefore, O ye kings: be instructed, ye judges of the earth. Serve the LORD with fear, and rejoice with trembling” (Ps 2:10-11).

6.2.2.en: * The blessed David urges the kings and those subject to him to run toward the Savior, and embrace His saving laws, so that they may reap benefit through the guidance of these laws and their teachings (cf. Ps 2:10)...

6.2.3.en: He is the King of us all, He whom they thought was the king of the Jews alone. “Serve the Lord with fear, and rejoice (exult) with trembling” (Ps 2:11). That is, those who rejoice and are glad in their salvation must not rely upon compassion alone, but must be in fear and trembling, along with the righteousness joined to them. The Holy Bible says: [Let him that thinketh he standeth take heed lest he fall] (cf. 1 Cor 10:12)... Now by saying “with trembling” He means “with remorse,” lest the joy that is in the Lord turn into joy in the world.

6.2.4.en: Theodoret, bishop of Cyrrhus: The prophet Daniel says: “He removeth kings, and setteth up kings: he giveth wisdom unto the wise, and knowledge to them that know understanding” (Dan 2:20-21).

6.2.5.en: “Authority” here means the power and what man enjoys, whether of wealth, position, knowledge or intelligence. All of these can be used for building up or for tearing down. Therefore wisdom is better than strength, because wisdom is able to direct strength toward building up. By divine wisdom the believer, through his union with God, enjoys the turning of even nature to his account, and the heavenly ones desire to serve him. By the wisdom who is the Lord Christ we say with the Apostle Paul: “I can do all things through Christ Jesus which strengtheneth me.”

6.2.6.en: In Christ Jesus the believer defies the devil and all the powers of evil, and even his enemies make peace with him. Evils and afflictions also turn to his good. “All things work together for good to them that love God.”

6.2.7.en: The more the believer’s possibilities, abilities and responsibilities increase, the more he needs humility, to draw from the wisdom of God, which alone is able to guide and support him.

6.2.8.en: * We are all equal by nature.

6.2.9.en: * (Humanity was originally created whole) each one has authority to manage his life with no master constraining him, to have a life without grief or toil; so what does it mean to be led except to be enslaved?!

6.2.10.en: * It is not nature but (the love of) authority that divided humanity into slaves and masters.

6.2.11.en: * God granted humanity the right of self-determination (the master has no right to control the life of the slave).

6.2.12.en: * He who submits to you by custom and law is equal to you in the dignity of nature.

6.2.13.en: * To divide creation, which by right of nature befits practicing equality, into slaves and a ruling power, one part commanding and the other submitting, is tyranny and usurpation of the order that God established.

6.2.14.en: * (Slavery is) a loss of the wholeness of the living being.

6.2.15.en: * The state of independence and freedom is the inclination of wisdom and the movement of man’s will.

6.2.16.en: * The highest problem of freedom is that man be master of himself.

6.3.0.en: St. Gregory of Nyssa: For being servants of His kingdom, you have not judged aright, nor kept the Law, nor walked after the counsel of God. [4]

6.3.1.en: The wise man presents the Law or the divine commandment to the leaders so that they may realize that they are servants of God, and that they must fulfill His will in their work of leadership. For the king, like every true believer, is God’s servant for good, feeling that his mission is not to dominate, but to support every person, if possible, in keeping the divine commandment.

6.4.0.en: He shall appear upon you in a terrifying and swift manner, for a judgment without pity shall be executed upon the eminent. [5]

6.4.1.en: Here the wise man addresses the leaders who work in the name of God, for they represent the stewardship of God, and it befits them to walk in Christ Jesus, that is, in the wisdom of God. So let them submit to the will of God and practice His commandment and lead their brethren to walk in Christ Jesus.

6.4.2.en: If kings think they are holders of authority, let them realize that the King of kings and Lord of lords will come, He who comes quickly, in great awe, to judge the great as well as the common; but without partiality He will be firmer still with those who have knowledge and authority, for He does not pity him who did not pity those subject to him.

6.4.3.en: For the small one is worthy of mercy.

6.5.0.en: But the mighty shall be mightily examined. [6]

6.5.1.en: The wise man warns those who work in the Lord’s vineyard that the owner of the vineyard, God Himself, comes suddenly and judges the world, beginning with the leaders. Whoever is small, that is, humble, draws forth God’s mercy; but whoever exploits his authority in pride and arrogance falls under eternal judgment, for judgment is without mercy to the one who has not used mercy. While of the merciful it is said: “Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy” (Mt 5:7).

6.5.2.en: * Not all men are judged in all matters without distinction among them, for it is said: “Mighty men shall be mightily tormented” (cf. Wis 6:6). And also: “He that knoweth his lord’s will, and prepareth not himself... shall be beaten with many stripes” (Lk 12:47). For greater knowledge is the basis of a more severe punishment. Therefore if the priest commits the same fault that those under his care commit, he does not bear the same punishment, but a graver punishment.

6.5.3.en: St. John Chrysostom: * If it can be said: “The mighty shall be mightily examined” (Wis 6:6), then what is required of me is more than what is required of the deacon, and what is required of the deacon is more than of the layman, and as for him who occupies the position of church leadership above us all, more is required of him.

6.5.4.en: Origen: When the monk Heliodorus (Helgiodorus) drew back from the perfect ascetic life and separated from St. Jerome, who had taken him with him to the East, he wrote him a severe letter rebuking him for this conduct. This letter had a strong effect in the West, so that some even memorized it, such as Fabiola, and in it he said: [To whom God entrusts much, of him more will be required (Lk 12:48). “For the mighty shall be mightily tormented” (cf. Wis 6:6). No one can boast on the day of judgment merely because he is chaste in body, for men will give account for every idle word (Mt 12:36).]

6.5.5.en: * Do you think that Ananias and Caiaphas and Judas the traitor, their crime is not greater than that of Pilate, who was compelled against his will to judge our Lord? The sin of Judas corresponds to his former merit, and the more heinous the crime the more severe the punishment, “for the mighty shall be mightily tormented” (cf. Wis 6:6).

6.6.0.en: St. Jerome: For the Lord of all shall not draw back before anyone, nor stand in awe of any man’s greatness; for He made both the small and the great, and He cares for all alike. [7]

6.6.1.en: No one escapes the general judgment, but all stand before the just Judge. Since He is the Creator of all and cares for all, He judges all without partiality, for all are the object of His love and care.

6.6.2.en: And as St. Basil the Great wrote to a fallen virgin, demanding that she remember that she will not escape judgment, like all other human beings.

6.6.3.en: * Remember your last day, for surely you will not be different from all the rest of women so as to live (here) forever.

6.6.4.en: Remember that catastrophe, the death rattle and its hour, the terrible word of God, the hastening of the angels on their way, the trembling of the soul in fear.

6.6.5.en: Remember the moment of dying, when the soul suffers because of the sense of sin, grieving over this present life while it must exist in the long life (the eternal)...

6.6.6.en: Picture to me, as you imagine it, the end of human life when the Son of God comes in His glory with His angels: “Our God shall come, and shall not keep silence” (Ps 50:3). He comes to judge the quick and the dead, and to give to every one according to his works; and when that dreadful trumpet sounds, all those who have fallen asleep through the generations come forth, and those who have done good come to the resurrection of life, and those who have done evil to the resurrection of judgment (Jn 5:29).

6.6.7.en: Remember the vision of Daniel, how he made clear before us the day of judgment: “I beheld till the thrones were placed, and the Ancient of days did sit, whose garment was white as snow, and the hair of his head like the pure wool... his throne was the fiery flame, a burning fire; a fiery stream issued and came forth from before him: thousand thousands ministered unto him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him: the judgment was set, and the books were opened...” (Dan 7:9-10).

6.6.8.en: He will proclaim openly before men and the good and the evil angels the open and the hidden things, the works of all and their words and their thoughts.

6.6.9.en: What then will those who live a wicked life do?!

6.6.10.en: Where will those souls hide whose shame will be exposed before all?!

6.6.11.en: With what body will these endure the unbearable pains in the fire that is not quenched and the worm that does not die, in the depths of the abyss where there are darkness and terror and bitter wailing and lamentation and weeping and gnashing of teeth without end?!

6.6.12.en: There is no room there for release from these woes after death, no counsel and no means of escape from the pain.

6.7.0.en: St. Basil the Great: But a strict inquiry awaits the mighty. [8]

6.7.1.en: God will judge every man according to his abilities, gifts and position, the things that were granted to him to work with for the account of his brethren in humanity, and not to use them in a spirit of selfishness as a private privilege. And according to the measure of the possibilities he received there awaits him an inquiry or reckoning commensurate with what he enjoyed.

6.8.0.en: Unto you therefore, O kings, I direct my words, that you may learn wisdom and not fall away. [9]

6.8.1.en: The wise man calls the kings to learn and enjoy wisdom instead of being haughty with authority and power, lest they fall into evil, and under judgment.

6.8.2.en: The wise man remains thirsty to learn as long as he is still in this life, even if he is a king or a spiritual leader. For there is no man who has no need of continual learning, so long as he is still in the body.

6.9.0.en: For those who keep in holiness what is holy are testified to be holy, and those who learn it find in it a defense. [10]

6.9.1.en: The weapon of kings is holiness, that they may imitate the holy King of kings. For by true holiness they stand rejoicing before the Holy One in the judgment. As St. Paul says: “To the end he may stablish your hearts unblameable in holiness before God, even our Father, at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ with all his saints” (1 Thess 3:13), “Follow peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord” (Heb 12:14).

6.9.2.en: He also calls them to listen to the counsel he offers them that they may be disciplined, that is, accept the Lord’s discipline with joy so as to bear the image of the Holy One.

6.9.3.en: * He who dreams that he is able to enter heaven without purity of heart and righteousness of life and holiness of body dies in this illusion, to awake and find himself in eternal shame and disgrace.

6.10.0.en: St. Irenaeus: Therefore desire my words, and long for them, that you may be instructed. [11]

6.10.1.en: As the wise man speaks in a spirit of love, in true longing for their growth and success, he asks them in a spirit of sincere brotherhood to desire his words, and to yearn for them or long for them, so that they may have true knowledge or fitting teachings.

6.10.2.en: He does not ask them for obedience, as one who commands so that they are bound to submit and carry out. Rather, in a spirit of love he guides and reveals the secrets of the successful life and of the way that leads them to eternal glories; therefore he begs them to review the matter, that their hearts may be kindled with longing toward the truth.

6.11.0.en: 13 For wisdom is bright and does not fade, and the beholding of her is easy for those who love her, and the finding of her is easy for those who seek her. 14 For she goes before and shows herself to those who desire her, 15 and whoever is early in seeking her does not labor, for he finds her sitting at his doors. 16 For meditation upon her is the perfection of prudence, and whoever watches for her sake will not long have care. 17 For she goes about seeking those who are worthy of her, and appears to them in the ways smiling, and meets them whenever they meditate upon her. 18 For the beginning of her is sincerity in the desire for discipline. 19 And the seeking of discipline is love, and love is the keeping of the laws, and the observing of the laws is the steadfastness of purity. 20 And purity brings near to God. 21 So the desire for wisdom brings to the Kingdom.

6.11.1.en: Wisdom is glorious, and never fadeth away: yea, she is easily seen of them that love her, and found of those who seek her. [12]

6.11.2.en: Here the wise man declares the nature of wisdom: on one side it is glorious, and its glories are not temporary but permanent and eternal, not fading. And on the other side it seeks after man, and announces its presence, and reveals itself to whoever loves it. It is easy to obtain and exceedingly simple, and ever present.

6.11.3.en: Truly it does not force itself, nor occupy a man’s heart by compulsion against his will; if he seeks it and asks for it, he finds it before him, longing to dwell in him.

6.11.4.en: Here he speaks of wisdom as being the Second Hypostasis, the divine Word, the Glorious, whose glory is everlasting and present in every place, whose delight is to abide in us while we abide in Him.

6.12.0.en: She goes before, and makes herself known to those who desire her. [13]

6.12.1.en: Along with the wonderful splendor of wisdom and its surpassing freshness, that is, its unceasing fruitfulness, those who love it and seek it recognize it, knowing it by practical experience and life.

6.12.2.en: He did not say that we are able to know wisdom, but that it makes itself known to whoever desires it. For man by his natural human abilities is unable to know divine wisdom. No one can say that Christ is Lord but by the Holy Spirit. No one experiences the sweetness of God’s wisdom and His powers and possibilities except him in whose heart love is poured out by the Holy Spirit (Rom 5:5).

6.12.3.en: Whoever possesses the Lord Christ knows Him and lives by Him and enjoys His divine wisdom, and truly becomes His ambassador.

6.13.0.en: And whoever seeks her early shall not labor much, for he shall find her sitting at his doors. [14]

6.13.1.en: The wise man calls us to long for wisdom and seek it, that it may be manifested in our hearts as on Mount Tabor. The secret of our weariness and our inability to discover the person of the Lord Christ and enjoy Him is that we do not rise early to Him. “I love them that love me; and those that seek me early shall find me” (Prov 8:17). Let Him be first in our hearts, our thoughts and our senses; no one and nothing shall occupy His place in us.

6.13.2.en: Wisdom, or the Lord Christ, on His part sits at our inner doors asking permission to enter. “Behold, I stand at the door, and knock: if any man hear my voice, and open the door, I will come in to him, and will sup with him, and he with me” (Rev 3:20).

6.13.3.en: * God gave us the Holy Spirit as an ally and mighty guardian, a great teacher of the Church, and a strong champion to help us. So do not fear the devils nor Satan, for He who fights for us is stronger than they.

6.13.4.en: Let us open our doors to Him, for He seeks those who deserve Him and searches out those to whom He is able to give His gifts.

6.13.5.en: St. Cyril of Jerusalem: Wisdom calls us to rise early in seeking Him, for none of the people in the wilderness could enjoy the manna that came down from heaven unless he rose early and gathered it before the rising of the sun.

6.13.6.en: He went before and took the initiative in love, He came to us Himself. In love He asks of the human soul, saying: “Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled: for my head is filled with dew, and my locks with the drops of the night” (Song 5:2). So if she despises Him, and prefers sleep to Him, and in sluggishness refuses to leave her bed to open the door to Him, she loses the opportunity of meeting Him, and we say: “I opened to my beloved; but my beloved had withdrawn himself, and was gone: my soul went out when he turned away: I sought him, but I could not find him; I called him, but he gave me no answer” (Song 5:6).

6.14.0.en: For meditation upon her is the perfection of wisdom, and whoever watches for her sake shall quickly be free from cares. [15]

6.14.1.en: Let us open our inner doors to our Savior by our solitude in quietness, contemplating our need of Him, and asking Him to enter and reveal Himself in us. We watch and refuse to sleep, saying with our father Jacob: “I will not let thee go, except thou bless me” (Gen 32:26).

6.14.2.en: For the way to wisdom is in our hands, indeed within us, and enjoying it is exceedingly easy, if we rise early to it, and forget everything for its sake. And we listen to its voice before every other voice.

6.14.3.en: The wise man asks of us a life of spiritual watchfulness, that is, concern for cleaving to the Lord, so that care cannot cleave to us, but we are freed from it and become in fellowship with the heavenly ones.

6.15.0.en: For she it is who goes about seeking those who are worthy of her, and in the ways appears to them with kindness, and in every thought of theirs comes to meet them. [16]

6.15.1.en: The wise man affirms the truth of the surpassing divine love, for though the divine Wisdom does not force our souls against our will, yet He stands at the door asking to enter into us. We on our part rise early to Him, declaring our desire to receive Him, and He on His part goes about as one searching for us, and appears to us in the midst of all our circumstances like one in the midst of the roads asking us to receive Him, and even declares Himself in our thoughts that we may long for it and desire His dwelling in us.

6.16.0.en: For the very true beginning of her is the sincere desire for discipline, and the care of discipline is love. [17]

6.16.1.en: The wise man offers us the ladder by which we ascend to enjoy wisdom; the five rungs of the ladder are:

6.16.2.en: a. Accepting discipline: The believer who longs for wisdom hates sin, and so accepts with joy what befalls him of discipline by divine permission, until sin becomes bitter in his mouth and he finds no pleasure in it.

6.16.3.en: b. By accepting the Lord’s discipline of him in sincerity and simplicity of heart, his heart opens more to the love of God. So the pleasures of the world do not occupy him, nor is he troubled by the toils of temporal life, but all his energies are absorbed in divine love.

6.16.4.en: c. As he loves God he keeps His commandments, and as the Lord Christ says: “He that hath my commandments, and keepeth them, he it is that loveth me” (Jn 14:13).

6.16.5.en: d. Whoever keeps the divine commandment, the commandment keeps him, so he bears the righteousness of Christ and appears before the Father justified freely, in purity and cleanness.

6.16.6.en: e. As the believer enjoys purity he cleaves to the Lord and sees Him. “Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God” (Mt 5:8).

6.17.0.en: And love is the keeping of her laws, and the observing of the laws is the assurance of incorruption. [18]

6.18.0.en: And incorruption makes us draw near to God. [19]

6.18.1.en: Wisdom grants people immortality and fellowship in the Kingdom of God.

6.18.2.en: Nothing occupies the heart of the wise man like drawing near to God and being with Him eternally, so he often speaks of immortality and incorruption, or non-death, in eternal life.

6.18.3.en: * Man is mortal by nature, because he was created from nothing, yet because he was created in the image of the One who is, it was possible for him to resist the power of natural corruption and remain in incorruption, had he kept God in his knowledge, as Wisdom says: “The keeping of the laws brings about incorruption” (Wis 6:18). And by being in a state of incorruption it was possible for him to live from then on as God (immortal), as the Holy Bible indicates when it says: “I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High. But ye shall die like men, and fall like one of the princes” (Ps 82:6-7).

6.19.0.en: St. Athanasius the Apostolic: Therefore the desire for wisdom leads to the Kingdom. [20]

6.19.1.en: * These emotions (longings) are evil if the love is evil, and good if the love is good. Let us prove this from the Holy Bible. The Apostle desires to depart and be with Christ (Phil 1:23). And it is said: “My soul breaketh for the longing that it hath unto thy judgments” (Ps 119:20). And also: “The desire (longing) for wisdom leads to the Kingdom” (Wis 6:20).

6.20.0.en: St. Augustine: If your delight be then in thrones and sceptres, O ye kings of the people, honor wisdom, that ye may reign for evermore. [21]

6.20.1.en: The wise man directs the eyes of kings to the eternal Kingdom, and its way is the enjoyment of wisdom.

6.20.2.en: Truly He set us up for God here to be kings and masters, but as we experience what we have of spiritual authority and possibilities in Christ Jesus, our heart is lifted up to heaven that we may enjoy with the King of kings and Lord of lords the heavenly royal glories.

6.20.3.en: Here we reign where we have authority over thought, heart, tongue and all the senses, and this is a pledge of the true heavenly Kingdom.

6.20.4.en: The wise man directs the eyes of kings to the eternal Kingdom: “that you may reign forever”?

6.20.5.en: Since some groups attacked the Old Testament and claimed that it did not point to the eternal Kingdom of Heaven, St. Augustine pointed to the passage before us along with other passages he cited from the Old Testament to affirm his call to the eternal Kingdom.

6.20.6.en: * It was truly said: “Love wisdom, that you may reign forever” (cf. Wis 6:21). If eternal life had not been clearly known in the Old Testament, the Lord would not have said to the unbelieving Jews: “Search the scriptures; for in them ye think ye have eternal life: and they are they which testify of me” (Jn 5:39). And to the same end came the words of the Psalmist: “I shall not die, but live, and declare the works of the LORD” (Ps 118:17). Again he says: “Lighten mine eyes, lest I sleep the sleep of death” (Ps 12:3). Again we read: “The souls of the righteous are in the hand of the Lord, and no torment shall touch them” (Wis 3:1). And immediately follows: “They are in peace, and though they suffered torment from men, their hope is full of immortality, and after a few chastisements they shall have great reward.” Again he says in another place: “But the righteous live for evermore; their reward also is with the Lord, and the care of them is with the most High: therefore shall they receive a glorious kingdom, and a beautiful crown from the Lord’s hand” (Wis 5:15-16).

6.20.7.en: These passages and many like them about eternal life, with greater or less plainness, are found in these writings. Even the resurrection of the body the prophets spoke of.

6.21.0.en: 22 If your delight be then in the throne and sceptre, O ye kings of the people, honor wisdom, that ye may reign for evermore, 23 and love the light of wisdom, ye that be rulers of the people. 24 And I will tell you what wisdom is, and how she came up, and I will not hide the mysteries from you, but I will seek her out from the beginning of her nativity, and make the knowledge of her plain, and not pass over any part of the truth, 25 neither will I go with consuming envy, for such a man shall have no portion in wisdom. 26 The multitude of the wise is the salvation of the world, and the wise king the upholding of the people, 27 therefore be instructed by my words, and profit by them.

6.21.1.en: And I will tell you what wisdom is, and how she came up, and I will not hide the mysteries from you.

6.21.2.en: But I will seek her out from the beginning of her nativity, and make the knowledge of her plain, and not turn aside from the truth. [22]

6.21.3.en: The writer identifies himself as Solomon who enjoyed the gift of wisdom, and so he cannot hide its mysteries, lest he be counted ungrateful for God’s gift, or one who does not love his brethren. He desires that every person get to know it, love it, ask for it from God its source, and possess it with him!

6.21.4.en: The true wise man walks in righteousness, in whose heart there is no place for selfishness, so he desires that all share with him in what he has received.

6.21.5.en: Wisdom is a spring of living waters; the more others drink from it, the more the spring keeps the purity of its water as it overflows without ceasing, so its water does not become stagnant, exposed to pollution with algae and microbes.

6.21.6.en: The writer wishes to reveal the Wisdom that comes from God, because confusion has occurred in the thoughts of many people, so they consider pleasure to be the happy life, and consequently wisdom is made to consist in the pleasures of the body and the enjoyment of temporal gifts and amusement, while the divine and heavenly things are in their minds imagination and illusion, which make man lose his reason and wisdom.

6.21.7.en: * The ordinary definition of wisdom is the seeking of what is good and the avoiding of evil. Therefore the Apostle is right in describing the wisdom of the flesh (as enmity against God) as a longing for goods that do not remain with man, where there is fear of losing these things one day when he leaves them behind. Such wisdom cannot be subject to the law of God. It must be crushed so that the wisdom of the Spirit may take its place, which does not place its hope in earthly goods and does not fear worldly evils. For the one nature of the soul has the wisdom of the flesh when it seeks the lower things, as it has the wisdom of the Spirit when it seeks the higher things, like the one nature of water, which freezes in the cold and melts in the heat.

6.21.8.en: St. Augustine: * As long as the flesh lives... no believer can delight in the will of God and carry it out actively in his life.

6.21.9.en: St. Gregory of Nyssa: * Fleshly wisdom is death, for sin is grave, and through sin death came. It is called wisdom though it is folly. For to worldly people sin, whether in thought or in deed, is counted wisdom, recognized as such although it is against the law of God, especially since those who sin are full of activity and intelligence.
